skills.name: areaOf
skills.card:
areaOf — Work out the space inside a shape — the area of a rectangle, square, circle, triangle, trapezoid, ellipse or parallelogram.
  needs: shape: string
  optional: width: number, height: number, side: number, radius: number, radius2: number, base: number, base2: number
  e.g. "area of a rectangle 8 by 5" → {"shape":"rectangle","width":8,"height":5}

shape.label: shape
shape.prompt: Which shape? (rectangle, square, circle, triangle, trapezoid, ellipse, parallelogram)

examples: area of a circle with radius 3
area of a triangle with base 10 and height 6
area of a square with 7 metre sides
area of a trapezoid with parallel sides 4 and 8, height 5

skills.name: perimeterOf
skills.card:
perimeterOf — Work out the distance round the edge of a shape — its perimeter or circumference, or how much fencing or edging it takes.
  needs: shape: string
  optional: width: number, height: number, side: number, sides: integer, radius: number, a: number, b: number, c: number
  e.g. "perimeter of a rectangle 8 by 5" → {"shape":"rectangle","width":8,"height":5}

shape.label: shape
shape.prompt: Which shape? (rectangle, square, circle, triangle, regularPolygon)

examples: circumference of a circle with radius 3
perimeter of a square with 7 metre sides
perimeter of a triangle with sides 3 4 5
perimeter of a hexagon with 5cm sides
how much fencing goes round a 10 by 7 plot
length of the edge of a square with side 6

skills.name: volumeOf
skills.card:
volumeOf — Work out the volume of a cube, box, sphere, cylinder, cone or pyramid.
  needs: solid: string
  optional: side: number, width: number, height: number, depth: number, radius: number
  e.g. "volume of a cube with 4cm sides" → {"solid":"cube","side":4}

solid.label: solid
solid.prompt: Which solid? (cube, box, sphere, cylinder, cone, pyramid)

examples: volume of a cube with 4cm sides
volume of a box 10 by 5 by 2
volume of a sphere with radius 3
volume of a cylinder radius 5 height 10
volume of a cone radius 3 height 9

skills.name: sleepCycleTimes
skills.card:
sleepCycleTimes — Work out wake or bedtimes a whole number of sleep cycles apart.
  needs: time: string
  optional: direction: string, cycleMinutes: integer, fallAsleepMinutes: integer
  e.g. "when should I go to bed to wake at 7am" → {"time":"07:00"}

direction.label: time given is
direction.description: wake = the time given is when you want to get up

examples: when should I go to bed to wake at 7am
if I go to sleep now at 23:00 when should I wake
wake times with a 100 minute cycle
bedtimes for a 08:00 alarm with no wind-down

skills.name: splitTimes
skills.card:
splitTimes — Work out the pace and split times needed to finish a distance in a target time.
  needs: distance: number, time: string
  optional: unit: string
  e.g. "split times for a 10k in 50 minutes" → {"distance":10,"time":"50:00"}

time.label: target time
time.prompt: What is the target time? Write it as 50:00 or 1:45:00.

examples: split times for a 10k in 50 minutes
what pace do I need for a 5k in 22:30

skills.name: sortList
skills.card:
sortList — Put a list of items in order — alphabetically, numerically, or in natural order where numbers inside names count.
  needs: items: array
  optional: by: string, direction: string
  e.g. "sort this list alphabetically" → {"items":["cherry","apple","banana"]}
examples: sort file names in natural order
order these names z to a

skills.name: fibonacci
skills.card:
fibonacci — Give the nth Fibonacci number, or the first n of them.
  needs: n: integer
  optional: mode: string
  e.g. "what is the 10th fibonacci number" → {"n":10}

skills.name: formatCurrency
skills.card:
formatCurrency — Write an amount of money the way a currency is normally written, with its symbol and decimal places.
  needs: amount: number, currency: string
  optional: style: string
  e.g. "write 1234.5 as pounds" → {"amount":1234.5,"currency":"GBP"}

currency.label: currency
currency.prompt: Which currency? (a three-letter code like GBP)

examples: show 42.5 euros with the code not the symbol

skills.name: formatNumber
skills.card:
formatNumber — Write a number with thousands separators, a set number of decimals, or in compact form like 1.2k.
  needs: value: number
  optional: decimals: integer, style: string
  e.g. "format 1234567 with thousands separators" → {"value":1234567}

value.label: number
value.description: for the percent style, a fraction: 0.15 is 15%

skills.name: toOrdinal
skills.card:
toOrdinal — Add the ordinal suffix to a number — 3 becomes 3rd, 42 becomes 42nd.
  needs: value: integer
  optional: style: string
  e.g. "write 3 as an ordinal" → {"value":3}
examples: write 21 as twenty-first style, with its ending
write 102 with its st nd rd th ending

skills.name: budgetSplit
skills.card:
budgetSplit — Divide an income into budget categories by percentage, using 50/30/20 or ratios you set.
  needs: income: number
  optional: preset: string, ratios: array, labels: array
  e.g. "split 3000 a month using 50/30/20" → {"income":3000}

income.label: amount to divide
income.prompt: How much is there to divide?

ratios.label: percentages
ratios.description: your own percentages, which must add to 100

labels.label: category names
labels.description: a name for each of your own ratios

skills.name: findOutliers
skills.card:
findOutliers — Spot the values sitting way off from the rest of a set.
  needs: values: array
  optional: method: string, threshold: number
  e.g. "find the outliers in these numbers" → {"values":[10,12,11,13,12,90]}
examples: find the outliers in these numbers
is anything way out of line in 8 9 10 11 50
which of these readings is off from the rest

skills.name: movingAverage
skills.card:
movingAverage — Smooth a series of numbers by averaging over a sliding window.
  needs: values: array, window: integer
  optional: type: string
  e.g. "3 point moving average of these numbers" → {"values":[1,2,3,4,5],"window":3}

window.label: window size
window.prompt: How many points should each average cover?

examples: 3 point moving average of these numbers
smooth these sales figures over 4 months
moving average of a noisy series
weighted moving average favouring recent points
moving average of a flat series

skills.name: rankValues
skills.card:
rankValues — Put numbers in order and give each its rank position.
  needs: values: array
  optional: labels: array, direction: string, method: string
  e.g. "rank these scores" → {"values":[90,70,85]}
examples: put these from best to worst: 72 95 88

skills.name: convertCase

style.label: case
style.prompt: Which case? (upper, lower, title, sentence, camel, pascal, snake, kebab or constant)

examples: make this title case: the lord of the rings
fix the capitals: HELLO THERE. HOW ARE YOU?
change my heading to title case: a tale of two cities
put this in upper case: quiet please

skills.name: diffText
skills.card:
diffText — Compare two versions of a text and show what was added and removed, by line or by word.
  needs: before: string, after: string
  optional: by: string
  e.g. "show me the line by line changes" → {"before":"apple
banana
cherry","after":"apple
blueberry
cherry"}
examples: show me the line by line changes
diff these two paragraphs by word
compare the old and new list
what was deleted from this list
show me what differs between the earlier draft and the later one
compare these two drafts line by line

skills.name: escapeHtml
skills.card: escapeHtml — Make text safe to drop into HTML, turning angle brackets and ampersands into entities — or turn escaped ones back. needs: text: string optional: direction: string e.g. "escape this html: bold" → {"text":"bold"}
examples: escape text with nothing special in it
make these angle brackets safe for a web page
encode the special characters so html shows them literally

skills.name: extractIpAddresses
skills.card:
extractIpAddresses — Find the IPv4 and IPv6 addresses in a server log.
  needs: text: string
  optional: unique: boolean, version: string
  e.g. "get the ip addresses from this log" → {"text":"from 192.168.1.10 to 8.8.8.8"}
examples: get the ip addresses from this log
find the ips in these lines
ignore a version number that looks like an ip

skills.name: extractListItems
skills.card:
extractListItems — Pull the bulleted or numbered list items out of a document.
  needs: text: string
  optional: type: string
  e.g. "get the list items from this note" → {"text":"Shopping:\n- milk\n- eggs\n- bread"}
examples: get the list items from this note
pull the items from a nested list
extract items from a mixed list

skills.name: extractNgrams
skills.card:
extractNgrams — Break text into overlapping runs of n words or characters — two-word runs, bigrams, trigrams.
  needs: text: string
  optional: n: integer, unit: string
  e.g. "get the bigrams from this sentence" → {"text":"the quick brown fox"}

text.label: text
text.prompt: Which text should I break up?

examples: get the bigrams from this sentence
split this into runs of two words
give me the three-word sequences in this

skills.name: maskSensitive
skills.card:
maskSensitive — Hide private details in text — emails, phone numbers, cards — behind placeholders.
  needs: text: string
  optional: style: string, kinds: array
  e.g. "redact the personal data in this" → {"text":"Contact ana@example.com or call 020 7946 0958."}

kinds.label: kinds to mask
kinds.description: limit the masking to these kinds

examples: redact the personal data in this
mask this card number with stars
scrub the email and phone number out of this
blank out the personal information here

skills.name: padText
skills.card:
padText — Pad text out to a fixed width, aligned left, right or centre.
  needs: text: string, width: integer
  optional: align: string, fill: string
  e.g. "pad "abc" to 8 characters" → {"text":"abc","width":8}
examples: pad with dots to make a table of contents line
pad text that is already too long

skills.name: reverseText
skills.card:
reverseText — Reverse a text — by character, by word, or by line.
  needs: text: string
  optional: by: string
  e.g. "reverse the word stressed" → {"text":"stressed"}
examples: reverse the word order of the quick brown fox

skills.name: slugify
skills.card:
slugify — Turn a title into a URL-safe slug — lowercase, hyphens, no accents or punctuation.
  needs: text: string
  optional: separator: string, maxLength: integer
  e.g. "make a slug from "Hello, World! A Beginner's Guide"" → {"text":"Hello, World! A Beginner's Guide"}

text.label: text
text.prompt: What should I turn into a slug?

examples: make a slug from "Hello, World! A Beginner's Guide"
url slug for "Café Münster — Opening Times"
slugify with underscores: My Blog Post
short slug, max 12 chars, from "The Complete Guide To Everything"

skills.name: sortLines
skills.card:
sortLines — Put the lines of a text in order — alphabetically, numerically, or by length.
  needs: text: string
  optional: by: string, direction: string, caseSensitive: boolean
  e.g. "sort these lines alphabetically" → {"text":"cherry\napple\nbanana"}
examples: sort this list z to a

skills.name: truncateText
skills.card:
truncateText — Cut text off at a maximum length and end it with an ellipsis.
  needs: text: string, limit: integer
  optional: unit: string, ellipsis: string, breakWords: boolean
  e.g. "shorten this to 20 characters" → {"text":"The quick brown fox jumps over the lazy dog","limit":20}

breakWords.label: cut mid-word
breakWords.description: allow cutting in the middle of a word

examples: truncate a string already short enough
shorten to 10 chars with a custom ellipsis
truncate mid-word if it has to

skills.name: formatCitation
skills.card:
formatCitation — Assemble a reference in APA, MLA or Chicago style from details you provide.
  needs: authors: array, title: string, year: integer
  optional: style: string, container: string, publisher: string, volume: string, pages: string, url: string
  e.g. "format this as an APA reference" → {"authors":["Jane Smith"],"title":"On measurement","year":2024,"container":"Journal of Things","volume":"12","pages":"3-19"}

container.label: journal, book or site
container.description: the journal, book or site it appeared in

examples: format this as an APA reference
make an MLA citation for this book
chicago style citation for a book
